headline: New Delhi: Thousands of supporters of the youth-led "cockroach" movement have been camping in the capital New Delhi to demand the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan
cluster_text:
New Delhi: Thousands of supporters of the youth-led "cockroach" movement have been camping in the capital New Delhi to demand the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra PradhanNew Delhi: Thousands of supporters of the youth-led "cockroach" movement have been camping in the capital New Delhi to demand the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, in the biggest public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term.

Here is a look at what sparked the protests and the situation now.

Why do protestors want Pradhan to quit?

The immediate trigger for the demonstrations was the cancellation of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), the undergraduate medical school entrance exam, after its question papers were found to have been leaked.

.The rise of the cockroaches! How CJI Surya Kant’s remark led to massive student movement in Jantar Mantar.

About 2 million students across the country took the exam on May 3, but it was later scrapped, with about a dozen student suicides linked to its cancellation.

A re-test was held in June.

Why is NEET important?

The exam is the sole gateway to undergraduate medical courses, and millions of aspirants sit for it every year, competing for fewer than 150,000 seats, making it one of the country's toughest entrance exams.

The situation is also symptomatic of broader strains on the country's higher education system, where grossly limited spots leave millions cramming for months, or even years, and high-stakes entrance exams leave many of them burnt out and in debt.

.'Not Protesters, Anti-Nationals': Manoj Muntashir slams CJP protest.

Have test papers been leaked before?

Exam question paper leaks are fairly common, and the NEET questions themselves were similarly leaked in some places in 2024, although a re-test was not ordered at the time.

Other examination papers have also been leaked, including those for recruitment of police constables and teachers.

Why is this leak different?

The exam leak this year coincided with the birth of the self-named Cockroach Janta Party satire movement, which appears to have channelled the frustration of the youth into the current protests.

.Shabana Azmi reveals she suffered asthma attack due to tear gas during CJP protest.

Experts say the group, which amassed millions of Instagram followers within days of being created in mid-May, tapped into the concerns of under-30s, who make up more than half the country's population, which include high youth unemployment and the latest exam paper leak.

How has the governmnet responded?

Pradhan says the government is committed to addressing the concerns of the youth and promised exam reforms, while Modi himself has vowed to punish those behind the leaks.

Health Minister J P Nadda met the protesters on Monday and sought time to discuss their demands, which also include the release of fasting activist Sonam Wangchuk, who was taken to hospital last week, and compensation of 10 million rupees ($104,000) each for the students who died by suicide after the exam leak.

What is the situation now?

Two days after tens of thousands of protesters attempting to march on parliament were met with tear gas and baton charges, thousands remain camped at the sit-in protest site in New Delhi, where the movement's leaders say they will remain until their demands are met.

Opposition groups, including the main opposition Congress party, have also vowed to raise their cause in and outside parliament, seeing it as a new opportunity to corner Modi and his party over an issue that has massive resonance and impacts Modi's youth vote base.

New Delhi: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) protests in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar have triggered a debate on the shifting paradigm in political communication.

Pundits have read it as a rise of the audio-video heavy Instagram as the most effective tool of communication to the masses. Whatapp is a passe, they feel.

The contemporary history of political communication, is replete with examples of how leaders have used social media to amplify their message. Effective communication, does not necessarily depend of the medium or affordance one uses. It’s the message, stupid! And not the messenger.

.Dharmendra Pradhan resignation: Narendra Modi’s first blink gives Opposition a big chance to recoup.

At the 2012 Republican Convention, iconic Hollywood actor director Clint Eastwood launched a 15-minute harangue at empty chair as if it was occupied by the Barak Obama.

President Obama, seeking a second term in office, responded with a terse X (previously Twitter) message that evoked a strong response from his supporters.

It was a picture of a monogrammed chair from the back with Obama sitting. The caption to the post was simple one liner- This seat’s taken.

.

Communication, especially political communication is about messaging- text, visual, audio or a mix of these. Technological interventions simply offer more affordances to the communicators to experiment and reach out to the people.

A good communication strategy is a rational decision making that factors in target audience to create authentic illusions.

Obama was the first world leader to tap into the potential of Twitter to reach out to his support base. And it did work well for him.

Former German Chancellor Angela Merkel instead relied on Instagram. Infact, it is said that she 'Merkelised' Insta to create what pollical scientist Julia Sonnevend and Olivia Steiert call “visually authentic performance.”

In research paper, the two academics, illustrate in some detail how Merkel evolved an image that was in sharp contrast to some of her contemporaries who were using populist rhetoric. The larger leitmotif of Merkel’s Insta posts were driven by “spontaneity, predictability, ordinariness, imperfection, ambivalence, confessions and immediacy.”

For instance, a July 2016 post is a close up of the shoes of Merkel and British PM Theresa May standing at the podium in which May’s bare legs in heels are juxtaposed with Merkel in black pants and slippers.

.

The picture depicts “authenticity and contrast.” And underlines Merkel’s image as a leader know for “rational, evidence-based-decision-making and skilled negotiations.”

Merkel is the not the only leader to make a effective use of Insta for political communication. Former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern posted regularly on Insta to strike a personal connect with the people.

But what worked for Merkel and Jacinda, may or may not work for the others. Every medium has a its own unique grammar. A good screenplay may or may not yield a good film.

Instagram is an audio-visual medium. Its medium where communicators uses pun, context, symbolism, borrows heavily from popular cinema to send across a message. A slight turn of a head, a background score may say lot more than a thousand words.

Moreover, in politics, the focus is now more on individuals around whom political narratives are built. These are personas assiduously evolved over decades in various phases of experimentation and consolidation of the imagery.

In reaching out to a new constituency, there is always the risk of losing the old.

BJP leader LK Advani tried to emulate Vajpayee by travelling to Pakistan after the 2004 defeat of the NDA. That neither helped his personal or his party’s cause.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: Amid ongoing protests over NEET-UG paper leak issue, govt Thursday named new secretaries for higher and school education departments, with incumbent Vineet Joshi, who had charge of both, moved to low-profile panchayati raj department.
While animal husbandry secretary Naresh Pal Gangwar was appointed the new secretary for higher education, TK Anil Kumar will be the new school education secretary. The changes mark an overhaul of sorts in 
education ministry bureaucracy, as 
Abhishek Singh was earlier named head of the 
National Testing Agency, which conducts NEET, CUET and other exams.
In early June, CBSE chief Rahul Singh and secretary Himanshu Gupta were transferred out of the National Testing Agency after a controversy over on-screen marking.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
The secretary-level appointments included 13 new department heads, including a bifurcation of ministry of housing and urban affairs. MoHUA secretary K Srinivas has been shifted to development of north eastern region (DoNER) ministry. D Thara, from Gujarat cadre, has been appointed secretary of the just-created department of capital development, while her batchmate Satendra Singh from Jharkhand will lead the department of urban development.
The changes in education ministry are significant as govt has said demand for removal of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan is not under consideration, but steps will be taken to address concerns. The appointments committee of cabinet also desginated Chandra Bhushan Kumar as new labour secretary, while Keshav Chandra will be the new mines secretary. Odisha cadre IAS officer SK Lohani has been designated as animal husbandry secretary.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: More than three years after Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives, Supreme Court was informed Friday that probes into only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by SITs of state police while CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.
Appearing for the CBI, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the central probe agency had filed chargesheets in 21 cases and closure reports in six, of which three had been accepted. It was continuing investigations into the remaining four cases.
Former Maharashtra DGP Dattatray Padsalgikar, who was appointed to oversee the investigations, informed the court through a report that of the 3,020 cases being probed by the SITs across eight districts, chargesheets had been filed in only 301 cases and trial had commenced in 10.
The CJI-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously. Given the volume of cases, SC mulled setting up special courts to try these exclusively. It sought responses to this from Manipur govt and the high courts of Assam and Manipur.
SC had transferred investigations into cases of rape-murder other heinous offence to CBI and shifted their trial to Guwahati. The central agency told the court that examination of witnesses residing in Manipur through video-conferencing was a challenge because of law-and-order situations, non-cooperation and language barriers as they spoke different dialects.
Senior advocate Ngangom Junior Luwang complained that no effort had been made to trace 30 missing people and without their remains, authorities were not issuing death certificates required for other purposes. SC asked him to approach Manipur high court.
Advocate Sharukh Alam submitted that land belonging to churches vandalised during the clashes were getting encroached upon and said govt had taken no steps to reconstruct them. Bhati said govt's priority was to reconstruct damaged dwelling units. The bench said govt was right to prioritise reconstructing houses but asked it to take steps to stop encroachment of places of worship.

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson 
Saurav Das on Saturday urged the Centre to accept the protesters' demands, alleging that the government was transporting tanks to Delhi while the student agitation continued.
"Ab aayega aur maza! The government must understand that it can either bomb the peaceful protesters using the tanks it is transporting to Delhi (I mean, what are they trying to do by transporting these? Kill their own children? Is this where we have come in Gandhi's India?) Or, accept demands. The time is ticking!" Das said in a post on X.

We will then decide on our next steps. If the government continues this approach, we will be forced to take a tough stance," Ranka said.
Earlier, activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh after the Union government gave a written assurance on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.

NEW DELHI: Aiming to ensure faster disposal of exam paper leak cases, govt has proposed a three-month deadline for respective high courts to dispose of appeals against orders of special fast-track courts, unlike other cases where no such fixed timeline for deciding appeals exists. This converts an open-ended investigation and judicial process into a time-bound one.
According to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill circulated to Lok Sabha MPs Saturday, individuals, service providers and organised gangs involved in paper leaks would face longer jail terms, steeper fines, and time-bound investigation and disposal of trials and appeals.
What changes in New Bill
As per the bill, which would be introduced in Lok Sabha Monday, the minimum jail term for offences committed by individuals, as well as directors, senior management personnel or persons in charge of service providers conducting public examinations, has been increased to five years. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
In cases involving organised crime, the minimum imprisonment has been proposed at seven years from the current provision of five years. In all these cases, the maximum jail term would be 10 years.
For speedy investigations, the bill proposes govt may constitute a central investigation agency or a special task force (STF). Where an STF has been constituted, it would carry out the investigation. The bill also seeks to insert a new provision mandating that every investigation be completed within two months.
The bill provides for day-to-day proceedings and empowers states to establish special fast-track courts in consultation with the chief justice of the respective HC.
It mandates that such trial proceedings shall continue until all witnesses in attendance have been examined. These courts would be required to dispose of cases within three months from the date of filing of the chargesheet. All pending trials will be shifted to the special court, and these must also be disposed of within three months.
It proposes that any appeal against an order of a fast-track court shall be heard by a division bench of HC. It proposes that every appeal be filed within 30 days from the date of the fast-track court's order and not after a maximum of 90 days under any circumstances.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: If the students' protest held the Modi govt hostage for a week, its potency was amplified by the political class that blockaded the Parliament alongside.
But the symphony was not perfect from the start as the anti-BJP bloc had two opposing streams. The one led by 
Congress viewed 
CJP with suspicion, haunted as it was by the spectre of the Anna Hazare agitation that became the nemesis of the Manmohan govt and was later found to have been orchestrated by RSS. But Left outfits and some regional parties backed CJP as the voice of the youth.
When the like-minded parties met an hour before the start of the monsoon session Monday, the NEET protest competed with "Ayodhya donation scam" row as the plank to be espoused.
Congress and SP argued that Ayodhya should be picked as the opening salvo against BJP. But a consensus emerged on taking up the "paper leak" protest first after a forceful push from other parties which argued that the opposition had to associate itself with the youth march to Parliament.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
For Congress, which had been protesting against "paper leaks" for two years, the issue of political credit was also a consideration. The AAP background of CJP founders Abhijeet Dipke and others made many sniff a conspiracy. But barely two hours later, the police crackdown on young marchers ended all equivocation.
All along, protesters were also actively courting political support. Activist 
Sonam Wangchuk, and later his wife Gitanjali Angmo, questioned Rahul's absence from Jantar Mantar, even as SP's Dimple and Akhilesh Yadav, Shiv Sena's Uddhav Thackeray and son Aditya, NCP-SP's Sharad Pawar, AAP's Arvind Kejriwal and scores of others visited the venue. 
CPI (ML)'s Dipankar Bhattacharya and CPM's M A Baby were among the first to lend support in early June.
Post-crackdown, the gap kept closing as the controversy intensified, crowds continued to swell and the story went global.
Amid scepticism about the newbie, Congress and opposition were assured by the fact that the Jantar Mantar stage of Dipke had been filled with student activists from the Left parties. It was evident in the way Rahul Saturday held a news conference with AISA activists to reiterate that protesters would not budge without the resignation of the education minister. It appeared to be a bid to queer the pitch for CJP, which was in talks with govt.
In the end, as Dharmendra Pradhan resigned, the political class and the Jantar Mantar platform were together in hailing it as a victory for the young seeking accountability from the govt.

NEW DELHI: State-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) spudded the first deepwater appraisal well in the Mahanadi offshore basin Friday, marking a key step in assessing the hydrocarbon potential of one of Indiaâs most prospective offshore regions and paving the way for higher domestic oil and gas production.
The well, named MN-DWN18-1-HD, is the first of four planned deepwater appraisal wells in the basin. The drilling programme, under govtâs Samudra Manthan mission, will use deepwater technology to evaluate the commercial viability of hydrocarbon reserves.
Building on the recent Utkal and Konark discoveries that have strengthened the hydrocarbon prospectivity of the Mahanadi offshore basin, ONGC said the well is being drilled around 23 nautical miles from the Konark discovery off the Odisha coast. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
Petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri, who flagged off the drilling virtually, said the exercise marks âthe beginning of a new chapterâ in Indiaâs efforts to strengthen energy security and reduce dependence on imported crude oil and natural gas.
India imports nearly 90% of its crude oil requirement and about half of its natural gas demand, making higher domestic production a key component of its long-term energy security strategy to reduce exposure to global supply disruptions and price volatility.
The appraisal drilling is expected to provide a clearer assessment of the basinâs resource potential before any commercial development is taken up.
The minister said a series of policy reforms over the past decade have reshaped the countryâs exploration and production sector. These include the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP), the Open Acreage Licensing Programme (OALP), a revenue-sharing regime, and opening nearly 99% of the countryâs previously restricted offshore âNo-Goâ areas for exploration.
According to the minister, about 81% of Indiaâs active exploration acreage has been awarded since 2014, reflecting increased investor interest following the reforms.
Puri said govt has also expanded geoscientific data generation through initiatives such as Mission Anveshan, the National Seismic Programme and the National Data Repository to improve exploration success in frontier basins.
Under OALP, 172 exploration blocks covering nearly 3.8 lakh sq km have been awarded so far, attracting committed investments of more than $4.3 billion. During 2025-26, around 674 exploration wells were drilled, five new hydrocarbon discoveries were made, and seven discoveries were brought into production, he said.

NEW DELHI: âJhukti hai duniya, jhukhane wala chahiyeâ : These are remarks by Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of Cockroach Janata Party, after Union education minister 
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday following massive sustained protests by students against NEET-UG examination paper leak.
"We have done it. Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned. And this resignation is proof that if you people are not afraid, if you people do not bow down to this government, then we can take the resignation of anyone," Dipke said, reacting to the big news.
 The Cockroach Janata Party was born out of a meme in May this year. In two months, it has ended up achieving what many political parties in the opposition space could not do in the last 12 years.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
In a letter shared on X, Pradhan announcing his resignation said, "The situation that has emerged at Jantar Mantar and elsewhere in the country should not be exploited by anti-national forces. The unity of the country must remain intact. The future of every student in India should not get entangled in legal complications."
The significance of this one resignation can be gauged if we rewind to the past and remember what Union minister 
Rajnath Singh had once said in the midst of the raging Lalit Modi controversy. 
The Congress was demanding resignations of some top BJP leaders for helping Lalit Modi leave the country. Rajnath Singh had then remarked: "Ministers here do not resign. This is not UPA; this is NDA."
The Congress-led UPA, which ruled the country from 2004 to 2014, saw resignations of several top ministers in two terms - some on charges of corruption, some for enforcing responsibility for administrative failures.
But since 2014, the situation has been different. There have been several controversies and protests in the last 12 years, but none was strong enough to achieve the resignation of the concerned ministers. Several top central ministers have been removed since 2014, but not one of them had to quit under any âprotest pressureâ. The only time Prime Minister Modi was perhaps under some pressure to remove his ministers was in 2021 when Union health minister Harsh Vardhan had to step down after public anger over the handling of the Covid crisis. But his exit was part of a larger Cabinet reshuffle that saw 12 ministers quit the Modi Cabinet. The exit of Ravi Shankar Prasad and Prakash Javadekar then also came as a surprise, but none of them were fallout of any protests.
 To that extent, Dipke and his movement have achieved what has been unthinkable in recent times. But while Dipke deserves to be credited for mobilising the students and keeping them focussed, his success perhaps may not have been possible without the active involvement of climate activist 
Sonam Wangchuk - whose 26-day hunger strike changed the dynamics of the Jantar Mantar protest.
Wangchuk, who walked into the protest with a rose flower in his hand, gave the biggest boost that the movement needed initially. His hunger strike ensured that the focus remained on the movement at a time when the government appeared reluctant to recognise or engage with the Jantar Mantar protesters.
Itâs a different matter though that the end of Sonum Wangchukâs fast on Thursday night, in the presence of two Union ministers, or rather in the absence of any CJP representative by his side in hospital, led to several questions being raised amid allegations of a deal with the Centre. The CJP welcomed the end of his fast but made it crystal clear that their protest will continue hinting at differences on the way forward. Such was the buzz and criticism that Sonam Wangchuk was forced to release a video message to take on his critics.
Little wonder then, Pradhanâs eventual resignation may perhaps be viewed and celebrated by some more as CJPâs victory and less as an outcome of Wangchukâs long fast. However, the fact remains that the two complemented each other for most part of the agitation.
Wangchuk welcomed Pradhanâs resignation and posted on X: "IT'S A VICTORY OF DEMOCRACY. direct democracy... straight from the streets. It's a victory of peace, patience & perseverance. Congratulations CJP, Gen Z of the nation and thank you all citizens for shedding fear and the fear of fear and rising up from every corner of the nation. FROM ACCOUNTABILITY, NOW TO REFORMS."
From meme to movement
It was on May 15 this year, the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, during a hearing reportedly said that some unemployed youngsters become journalists, RTI activists or social media users and "start attacking everyone". The CJI later clarified that his remarks had been misquoted and were not meant as a criticism of unemployed youth in general. He said he was referring specifically to people entering professions with fake or bogus degrees, and added that reports suggesting he demeaned youth were "totally baseless".
 Timeline of CJP mobilising from a meme to a movement
But by the time clarification came it was perhaps too late.
On May 16, a day later, Abhijeet Dipke, who had previously worked as a communications strategist with the Aam Aadmi Party, launched the Cockroach Janata Party as a satire movement. He launched a website with the tagline âVoice of the Lazy & Unemployed.â
Dipke described it as a platform for âall the 'cockroaches' out thereâ, with eligibility criteria listed as being unemployed, lazy, chronically online, and able to rant professionally. The satirical post gathered momentum as anger built over the NEET-UG paper leak, and Dipke flew back to India in early June to lead protests near Jantar Mantar in person.
Dipkeâs return was viewed with a lot of skepticism. His biggest challenge was to prove that online following could be translated on the ground into offline support. Dipkeâs movement got a boost from several other social activists and also Wanghchuk. On July 25, Dipke and his movement tasted thier first big success when Dharmendra Pradhan was forced to resign due to students protest
Dipke had an immediate message for the CJI: âI thank CJI Kant for calling us cockroaches. Had you not called us cockroaches, Pradhan would not have resigned.â

The success of this studentsâ protest also has a harsh message for the opposition parties, which did their best to own and influence the movement. While several parties and their leaders joined forces with Dipke and the student protesters at Jantar Mantar, the main opposition party Congress used guerilla tactics to hog the limelight and took the protests to the doors of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The fact that the opposition parties did play a small role in piling pressure on the government cannot be denied. The monsoon session of Parliament was under way and all senior opposition leaders were beginning to rally around the protesters perhaps to be seen and counted.

After the farmersâ protest of 2021 which pushed the Modi government on the backfoot and forced the NDA to repeal the three farm laws, this is the second successful protest to put pressure on the government. Newly appointed Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi said on Saturday he accepted the responsibility with a "sense of duty and humility," hours after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from the post following weeks of student protests over the NEET paper leak controversy.
"I have just got to know that the Prime Minister has given me a responsibility. I accept this responsibility with a sense of duty and humility," Joshi told reporters.
Joshi, who continues as Consumer Affairs Minister, has been given additional charge of the Education Ministry. He said he would try to perform to the best of his capacity under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's guidance.
"In the last 12 years of Prime Minister Modi's government, many historical achievements have been made. In the last four-five years, Dharmendra Pradhan also executed the National Education Policy," he said.
Pradhan resigned earlier Saturday, taking moral responsibility for the NEET controversy that sparked nationwide protests and a 36-day sit-in at Jantar Mantar by the Cockroach Janta Party. He said it was not a matter of "individual prestige" for him and he was disturbed to see the series of events that had unfolded.
The CJP called off its protest after the government accepted its key demands, including Pradhan's resignation, withdrawal of FIRs against peaceful protesters and financial compensation to families of NEET suicide victims.
Himachal Pradesh chief minister and Congress leader Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu criticised the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led central government on Saturday over the NEET paper leak, stating that Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, has become the voice of the students' fight for justice.
While addressing journalists after leading a candlelight march regarding the NEET exam paper leak -- which included Congress leaders, party workers, the Communist Party of India (Marxist) and the general public -- he said that ensuring transparency and fairness in matters concerning the youth's future was of utmost importance.
They raised slogans against the central government, demanding justice for the students during the march, which started from the Indira Gandhi Sports Complex and concluded near the Mahatma Gandhi statue on the Ridge.
The Cockroach Janta Party said its concerns and demands have been addressed after Union Minister Pralhad Joshi was given additional charge of the Education Ministry, following Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.
"Our concerns and demands have been addressed. Those demands resonated with the youth across the country, which is why this movement gained nationwide support," CJP Chief Spokesperson Saurav Das said.
"Whoever becomes the Education Minister should know that the youth are watching. They will demand accountability. So, when the time comes, work in the interest of the youth. Stop paper leaks and implement our five-point recommendations outlined in the demand charter," he added.
Das said the CJP will meet the new Education Minister very soon. "The government has promised to hold a meeting within a month, and then we will see what happens."
The CJP had been protesting at Jantar Mantar since June 20, demanding Pradhan's resignation over the NEET paper leak controversy. The protest was called off after the government accepted the party's demands.
Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati on Saturday termed Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation "appropriate", and said it would have been better had this step been taken earlier.
In a post on X in Hindi, Mayawati said, "The decision by Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign today, in the wake of the protests by students and youth, is appropriate, though it would have been better had this step been taken earlier. Furthermore, our party expects the Central Government to take strict action against the police personnel who brutally assaulted -- using batons and sticks -- the unarmed young men and women peacefully protesting at Jantar Mantar, leaving many of them seriously injured."
She said the male police personnel who engaged in indecent and shameful misconduct and used force against the female protesters must be identified.
"Strict legal action, including disciplinary proceedings and criminal cases, should be initiated against them to ensure no one dares commit such heinous acts in the future," she said.
Mayawati asked the government to withdraw FIRs or complaints filed against the protesting students and youth.
"This would spare them the ordeal of making repeated rounds of police stations and courts and thereby fostering an atmosphere of harmony in the country," she said.
Against the backdrop of high-voltage political drama, nationwide protests, and the recent resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, the Central Government is set to introduce the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha on Monday.
Union minister Dr. Jitendra Singh will move for leave to introduce the legislation. The Bill introduces seven key amendments designed to plug enforcement loopholes, establish dedicated judicial mechanisms, and accelerate criminal trials following widespread irregularities in the NEET-UG 2026 examination.
The legislative push comes after a complete washout of the ongoing Monsoon session of Parliament, which commenced on July 20, as opposition parties and student groups maintained unrelenting pressure on the Centre over paper leaks.
The proposed legislation seeks to significantly overhaul the original 2024 framework by instituting strict time bounds for both investigations and judicial proceedings.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: Saturday witnessed a series of major developments in the NEET paper leak controversy, beginning with Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation after weeks of nationwide protests. 
Hours later, Pralhad Joshi was appointed as the new education minister getting additional charge apart from portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution. 
Meanwhile, the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party (
CJP) held a third round of talks, after which the government agreed to withdraw FIRs filed against peaceful protesters. 
Following the meeting, the CJP announced the immediate withdrawal of its 36-day agitation at Jantar Mantar, saying it was ending the protest in "good faith" after the government accepted its key demands. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
The protest site was cleared after the CJP demands were met. 
The developments marked the biggest political fallout of the NEET controversy, which triggered nationwide student protests, a CBI probe and sweeping reforms to India's examination system.
Here are the top developments:Pralhad Joshi gets additional charge of education ministry
Hours after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, President Droupadi Murmu assigned senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi the additional charge of the Union education ministry on the advice of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. 
A five-time Lok Sabha MP from Karnataka's Dharwad, Joshi will continue to hold the portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution. He takes charge at a crucial time as the government rolls out reforms following the NEET-UG paper leak, including restructuring the NTA, tightening exam security and shifting NEET to computer-based testing from 2027.
After being given the charge, Joshi said: "The Prime Minister has placed his trust in me and has entrusted me with such a significant responsibility. With complete humility and a strong sense of responsibility, I will fulfil this duty...I thank the Prime Minister for giving me this important responsibility and for showing such great confidence in me. Under his guidance and leadership, I will work sincerely and try my best to meet his expectations in this department. With full dedication, humility, and honesty, I will work towards fulfilling this responsibility. I once again thank the Prime Minister for giving me this opportunity."
Metro stations reopen after protest ends
Normal Metro access resumed across Delhi after the CJP called off its 36-day protest, with the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) reopening the entry gates of all stations that had been closed because of security arrangements.
The reopening came shortly after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the Centre reached an agreement with the CJP to end the agitation. 
Earlier in the day, the DMRC had resumed services at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House and Central Secretariat stations before restoring entry and exit at all 18 affected stations, which had been placed under restrictions due to the protests near Jantar Mantar.
 Pradhan resigns, cites moral responsibility
Announcing his resignation in a letter addressed to the country's youth, Pradhan said he had submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi after considering the situation that had developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country.
He said he had spent more than four decades working for students, teachers and education reforms and had always believed that a strong education system was the foundation of a strong nation. Pradhan said the government acted immediately after irregularities surfaced in the NEET-UG examination by handing the investigation to the CBI, cancelling the examination and announcing a fresh test, while also deciding to shift NEET to computer-based mode from next year.
He added that he had accepted responsibility from the very beginning and had worked to ensure that no deserving student suffered because of what he described as an examination mafia. 
Recalling the events of the past few days had deeply saddened him, Pradhan said he was stepping down to prevent anti-national forces from exploiting the situation, safeguard national unity and allow students to focus on their education.
 Centre and CJP reach agreement after third round of talks
Hours after Pradhan's resignation, the Centre and the Cockroach Janta Party held a third round of talks, following which the student group announced the immediate withdrawal of its 36-day protest.
Addressing a joint press conference with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, CJP spokespersons Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das said the agitation was being withdrawn in good faith after the government accepted its key demands.
The CJP said its primary demand, Pradhan's resignation, had been fulfilled. It also said the Centre had agreed to withdraw FIRs and legal cases against peaceful protesters and assured that no retaliatory action would be taken.
  The government further agreed to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide in accordance with existing rules and regulations and promised to consider the CJP's five-point charter on examination reforms.
JP Nadda said the government had sympathetically considered the delegation's demands and would hold further discussions on long-term reforms to strengthen the examination system.
Student movement ends after 36 days
The CJP protest began at Jantar Mantar on June 20, demanding accountability over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak, wider reforms in the examination system and Pradhan's resignation.
 The movement gained national attention after climate activist 
Sonam Wangchuk joined the agitation with an indefinite hunger strike. His deteriorating health and later hospitalisation intensified public attention and increased pressure on the government.
Although Wangchuk ended his 26-day fast after receiving written assurances from the Centre, the CJP continued its protest until Pradhan resigned and the remaining demands were addressed.
Speaking after the agreement, Ashutosh Ranka appealed to protesters across the country to withdraw peacefully, while Saurav Das said the movement was ending with the understanding that all commitments would be implemented within the agreed timelines.
"Government accepted all our demands after 36 days of protest; we urge everyone to peacefully withdraw from protest sites," CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said.
Earlier in the day, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had briefly said the protest would continue until all demands were accepted. After the talks concluded, however, the organisation announced the end of the agitation.
Dipke also urged supporters not to treat Pradhan's resignation as a personal victory for him, saying the movement was driven by thousands of young people and should remain focused on institutional reforms rather than individuals.
Amit Shah reacts to Pradhan's exit
Union home minister Amit Shah reacted to Dharmendra Pradhan's exit as education minister saying, "Modi government respects youth's sentiments". 
"For BJP workers, the country, our youth, and students are far more important than any position. Today, the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan ji from his post exemplifies this very principle. The Modi government respects the sentiments of the country's youth and is committed to implementing the necessary reforms against paper leaks. The decisions taken by Modi ji to ensure strict punishment for those guilty of paper leaks are commendable. I am fully confident that these steps will ensure complete justice for the students who succeeded in the NEET examination.," he said.
"During his tenure, Shri Dharmendra Pradhan ji has brought about significant reforms in the effective implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), arrangements for examinations in mother tongues, expansion of PM SHRI Schools, promotion of digital education, skill development, and strengthening industry-academia coordination. His efforts toward making the examination system more inclusive and student-centric have also been noteworthy. His tenure is a testament to his dedication to the resolve of making India a developed nation," he added.
Opposition calls it a victory for students
The opposition described Pradhan's resignation as a major victory for students and renewed calls for broader reforms in the education system.
Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi called the resignation "the victory of the future of India", saying Pradhan had become a symbol of corruption, incompetence and the decline of the country's education system. 
He said the government must now introduce meaningful reforms and alleged that the issue of police action against student protesters would remain a key matter during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge termed the resignation a "victory of truth" and said Prime Minister Narendra Modi should apologise to the country's youth while ensuring action against those responsible for the alleged use of force against protesters.
AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal described the development as a "big win for democracy", while Karnataka chief minister DK 
Shivakumar said the Congress would continue raising issues concerning students and maintained that peaceful protests were an essential part of democracy.
Wangchuk welcomes outcome
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk welcomed the developments, describing them as "a victory of democracy, direct democracy, peace, patience and perseverance". He congratulated the student movement and thanked citizens across the country for supporting the agitation.
His wife, Gitanjali Angmo, also praised the role played by India's younger generation, saying the protests had demonstrated courage, patriotism and commitment to democratic values without violence.
Tougher anti-paper leak law proposed
The Centre has proposed major amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act to ensure faster investigations, time-bound trials and stricter punishment for paper leaks and examination malpractice.
The proposed Bill provides for the creation of Special Task Forces (STFs) to investigate offences, completion of investigations within two months, day-to-day hearings in special fast-track courts and disposal of appeals by High Courts within three months.
It also significantly increases penalties, proposing jail terms of up to 10 years and fines of up to Rs 10 crore for organised paper leak rackets, along with tougher action against service providers and officials found involved in examination fraud.
Biggest political fallout of NEET controversy
Pradhan's resignation marks the most significant political consequence of the NEET-UG paper leak controversy, which began after allegations of question paper leaks in the May 3 examination.
The controversy led to the cancellation of the examination, a nationwide CBI investigation, repeated protests, parliamentary disruptions, changes to the anti-paper leak law and a major restructuring of the National Testing Agency.
Pradhan also removed education minister from his X bio following the resignation.

NEW DELHI/BHUBANESWAR: 
Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation Saturday marks an unusual stumble in a political career that appeared to be headed towards more important destinations.
The architect of BJP's maiden victory in 
Odisha and facilitator of a series of wins elsewhere was first catapulted into the limelight while leading an ABVP-backed agitation in 1996 against an alleged Class XII question paper leak in Od-isha, during which he was injured in a police lathicharge.
Four years later, he won the Pallahara assembly seat on a BJP ticket. He became president of BJP's youth wing, BJYM, in Odisha in 2001 and was elevated as party national secretary in 2002. In 2004, he was appointed BJYM national president.
It was also the year he first entered Lok Sabha from Deogarh, when BJP and BJD were allies. Disappointment followed when he lost the assembly poll from Pallahara in 2009 after delimitation abolished the Deogarh LS seat and the alliance collapsed.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
Pradhan made a comeback when he was appointed co-in-charge of BJP's campaign for 2010 Bihar assembly polls, which BJP swept along with JDU. His nomination to Rajya Sabha from Bihar was seen as a just reward. As election in-charge of Bihar for the 2014 LS polls, he was crucial to NDA's sweep of 31 of its 40 LS seats.
Reforms in education under Pradhan
In 2014 he was inducted into Modi's first cabinet as MoS with independent charge of the petroleum ministry, despite resistance. 
Three years later, he was cabinet minister.
Amid the controversy over gas pricing, Pradhan launched a clean-up drive and put an end to the complete drip of corporate houses in the sector. His ministry's Ujjwala scheme helped expand LPG access. His work helped him get the education portfolio in 2021.
Pradhan's background as a grassroots worker also made him a crucial player in political battles. In 2022, he was made the party's election in-charge in UP, where BJP won 255 of 403 seats. In 2024, he successfully contested from Sambalpur. Though he retained the 
education ministry in Modi's third term, the reward was seen as less than what he deserved, considering he was the architect of BJP's organisational base in Odisha - a state where the party swept to office for the first time.
But things have been challenging for him since then, with paper leaks in 2024 and 2026, as well as the botched-up OMR rollout by CBSE.
In between, he delivered a success in Haryana in 2024, and Bihar, where he was BJP's election in-charge in 2025.

NEW DELHI: The West Bengal government on Saturday invoked its newly enacted "Goonda Act" against those accused of orchestrating violence during Friday's NEET protest, marking the first use of the legislation since it was passed by the state assembly.
The West Bengal Public Safety and Control of Anti-social Activities Act, 2026, was passed by the assembly recently after a stormy debate and criticised by the opposition as draconian.
Governor RN Ravi approved the legislation earlier this week.
Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announced the move on Saturday.
"I condemn the attack on our journalist friends on behalf of the entire House. An attack on journalists is unacceptable. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
We will take such action under the Goonda Act that these goons and even their next three generations will remember it. This is precisely why this law was enacted," Adhikari said in the assembly.
He informed the House that around 70 people identified from the Dharmatala rally were "not students" and had no connection with the agitation over the NEET paper leak.
Seven FIRs were registered over Friday's violence â six at Hare Street police station and one at Entally police station â with provisions of the new law incorporated into the cases, he told the House.
"The police exercised maximum restraint despite repeated provocation. That was the clear instruction given to them. They did not fall into the trap," Adhikari said.
The chief minister alleged that the rally initially proceeded peacefully before "anti-social elements" entered from behind and attempted to trigger violence.
According to him, the protest was organised under the banner of the "United Cockroach March", announced by what he described as a self-proclaimed member of the CJP, with participation from Left and ultra-Left student organisations, including the SFI, DSO, DYSA and AISF.
"In a democracy, everyone has the right to protest peacefully within the framework of law. The police were specifically instructed not to act unless the situation went completely out of control," he added.
Adhikari alleged that as the procession reached Dorina Crossing at Esplanade, shoes and water bottles were hurled first at policemen and then at journalists covering the demonstration.
"They wanted the police to resort to lathi-charge and tear gas. They wanted a spectacle. But Kolkata Police did not provide them that opportunity. The restraint shown by the force deserves appreciation," he stated.

NEW DELHI: Tightening the noose around individuals, service providers and organised gangs involved in paper leaks, the Centre has proposed longer jail terms, steeper fines, and time-bound investigation and disposal of trials and appeals.
According to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill circulated to Members of Parliament, the minimum jail term for offences committed by individuals, as well as directors, senior management personnel or persons in charge of service providers conducting public examinations, has been increased to five years. In cases involving organised crime, the minimum imprisonment has been proposed at seven years.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
The Bill proposes that any person resorting to unfair means or committing offences under the law shall be punished with imprisonment of at least five years, which may extend to 10 years, along with a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh.
It also proposes that any service provider found guilty would face a fine of up to Rs 5 crore â a five-fold increase over the existing provision â and would be barred from conducting public examinations for eight years, compared with the current four-year debarment.
If an investigation establishes that an offence was committed with the consent or connivance of any director, senior management personnel or person in charge of a service provider, such individuals would be liable to a minimum imprisonment of five years, extendable up to 10 years. The proposed maximum fine has also been increased from the existing Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore.
Seeking to amend Section 11 of the 2024 Act dealing with organised crime, the Bill proposes that if a person or group of persons, including an examination authority, service provider or any other institution, commits an organised crime, the minimum jail term would be increased to eight years from the current five years. The maximum penalty would also be raised tenfold to Rs 10 crore.
To ensure speedy investigations, the Bill proposes that the government may constitute a Central Investigation Agency or a Special Task Force (STF). Where an STF has been constituted, it would carry out the investigation. The Bill also seeks to insert a new provision mandating that every investigation be completed within two months.
For faster trials, the Bill provides for day-to-day proceedings and empowers states to establish Special Fast Track Courts in consultation with the Chief Justice of the respective High Court. It mandates that trial proceedings shall continue on a day-to-day basis until all witnesses in attendance have been examined.
The Special Fast Track Courts would be required to dispose of cases within three months from the date of filing of the chargesheet.
The Bill further proposes that any appeal against an order of a Special Fast Track Court shall be heard by a division bench of the High Court, which must dispose of the appeal within three months. It also mandates that every appeal be filed within 30 days from the date of the order.

NEW DELHI: The government has debunked doctored videos circulating on social media that wrongly showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi making threatening remarks against those protesting at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar over perpetual NEET paper leak. The Press Information Bureau (PIB) fact check unit said the clips were AI-generated deepfakes and did not reflect the Prime Ministerâs actual statements.
In related fact-checks, the government also flagged manipulated videos of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and commerce minister Piyush Goyal that were circulating on social media, falsely portraying them as making similar remarks against protesting students.
In a post on X, the PIB fact check unit said, âPakistani propaganda accounts are circulating a video of Prime Minister @narendramodi featuring fabricated statements that he never made regarding the protest in Delhi.â
It added, â#PIBFactCheck: This is an '#AI-generated deepfake video' shared to mislead the public. Prime Minister Narendra Modi did NOT make any such statement.â
The fact-check unit said the original video shared by PM Modi had been digitally altered to create a misleading version. 
It further shared a link to the original, unedited video posted by the PM.
The fake video circulating online showed an altered audio track in which PM Modi was allegedly made to say, "We are warning people against participating in the Cockroach Janata Party protest. Those who defy this warning will face strict action from the Government of India to ensure that such behaviour is not repeated in the future. Students are advised to focus on their education, failing which they will be compelled to face serious consequences. We are issuing a clear warning to the students."
The original video, posted by PM on his official social media account on Thursday, has since garnered 334 million views on Instagram. In the video, PM Modi addressed viewers as âFriendsâ and spoke directly into what appeared to be a phoneâs front camera, held at armâs length, with no podium, studio setup or formal backdrop.
In the video, the PM said the paper leak issue had caused difficulties for lakhs of students and their parents. He said those responsible had been arrested and that steps were being taken to ensure students did not lose an academic year.
The Prime Minister also said provisions for fast-track courts had been prepared and would be taken up by the Union cabinet.
The fact check unit also debunked another AI-generated video that falsely showed the PM similar remarks about the cockroach janata party protests. In this manipulated clip, Modi appeared to say, âWhat is the problem with these cockroaches? Even if one paper gets leaked, what is the big deal? Students can simply appear for the examination again next year.â The PIB clarified that the remarks were fabricated and shared the original video, which showed the Prime Minister speaking about the monsoon and the ongoing Monsoon session of parliament.
Additionally, the PIB flagged another digitally altered video of Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan that falsely portrayed him threatening protesting students. The manipulated clip appeared to show Pradhan saying that âbig leaders do not resign because of these cockroaches; they crush them under their shoes and throw them into dirty drains where they belongâ and warning that protesters would âsoon face grave consequencesâ. Refuting the claims, the PIB said, âUnion Minister Dharmendra Pradhan did not make any such statement.â
The fact-check unit blamed Pakistani propaganda accounts for circulating the digitally altered video containing fabricated claims. The original video was posted on the occasion of Sital Sasthi and made no reference to the protests.
The manipulated clip surfaced amid continuing protests led by the CJP, which has consistently demanded that Pradhan be held accountable for the alleged NEET paper leaks and has called for the education minister's resignation as one of its principal demands.
In another fact check, the government flagged a separate manipulated video involving commerce minister Piyush Goyal, which falsely claimed that Goyal had made similar threatening remarks against Jantar Mantar protests.

NEW DELHI: A potential new treatment for cervical pre-cancer and two next-generation vaccines against typhoid and other gut infections have moved a step closer to becoming available in India after the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) licensed the technologies to Indian pharmaceutical companies. If successful, the indigenous products could improve access to affordable treatment and vaccines while reducing dependence on imported technologies.
The technologies have been transferred under ICMRâs Medical Innovations Patent Mitra initiative, which helps convert government-funded research into products that can be developed, tested and eventually brought to the market.
Among them is SHetA2, a potential treatment for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN), a precancerous condition caused by persistent infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV). If left untreated, CIN can progress to cervical cancer, one of the leading cancers among Indian women.
Unlike surgery, which is commonly used to remove abnormal cells, SHetA2 is designed to selectively destroy HPV-infected abnormal cells while sparing healthy cells. Scientists believe it could offer women a safer and less invasive treatment option in the future. The technology has been licensed to Emcure Pharmaceuticals for further development, clinical testing and commercialisation.
ICMR has also licensed two vaccine technologies developed by its National Institute for Research in Bacterial Infections (NIRBI), Kolkata, to Biological E. One is a next-generation vaccine against typhoid, while the other is designed to protect against typhoid, paratyphoid and Shigella, bacteria that cause severe diarrhoea and other intestinal infections, particularly among children.
The vaccine candidates will now undergo further development and evaluation before they can be considered for regulatory approval and public use.
Dr Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research, and Director General, ICMR, said partnerships between researchers and industry are helping move promising discoveries from laboratories to patients while strengthening Indiaâs biomedical innovation ecosystem.
The technology transfer is part of ICMRâs broader effort to support indigenous healthcare innovation through patent protection, technology licensing, clinical validation and regulatory facilitation, with the aim of making affordable medicines and vaccines available to patients.

But while productivity has gone up, so has an invisible workplace problem - cervical pain.
full_text:
For millions of Indians, the workday begins with a laptop and ends with one. Eight to ten hours at a desk, endless video calls, back-to-back meetings and constant screen time have become the new normal. But while productivity has gone up, so has an invisible workplace problem - cervical pain.
Doctors say they are seeing a sharp rise in young professionals in their 20s and 30s walking into clinics with neck pain, stiffness, headaches and posture-related disorders. What was once considered an age-related condition is now increasingly becoming an occupational hazard of desk jobs.
The growing dependence on laptops, smartphones and sedentary lifestyles has turned cervical pain into a modern workplace health challenge. Beyond physical discomfort, it is affecting productivity, mental well-being and healthcare costs, raising concerns about whether India's rapidly expanding desk workforce is paying too high a price for long hours behind a screen.
Understanding cervical pain Cervical pain refers to pain or discomfort in the neck (cervical spine) and surrounding areas, including the shoulders and upper back. It can range from mild stiffness to severe pain and, in some cases, may be accompanied by headaches, tingling or numbness in the arms if nerves are affected.
While cervical pain can occur at any age, it is becoming increasingly common among young adults due to prolonged screen time, poor posture and sedentary lifestyles.
According to a study published in 
The Lancet, nearly 200 million people worldwide were living with cervical pain in 2020. The study projects that this number could rise to 270 million by 2050, driven by ageing populations, sedentary lifestyles and changing work patterns.
The impact extends well beyond physical discomfort. The World Health Organization (WHO) says musculoskeletal disorders are among the leading causes of work-related disability and absenteeism worldwide, affecting productivity and quality of life across age groups.
A Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2019 analysis estimated that around 1.71 billion people globally live with disorders such as neck pain, low back pain, fractures, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and other musculoskeletal conditions.
Is cervical pain becoming a workplace epidemic?To understand how widespread the problem is, we spoke to 30 working professionals about their work habits, posture and neck health. Their responses point to a common pattern: long sitting hours, few breaks and recurring cervical pain.
Most of the respondents were young professionals. 26 of the 30 participants were between 24 and 35 years of age, underscoring that cervical pain is increasingly affecting younger employees rather than just older adults.
Ten respondents experienced cervical discomfort every month, nine reported symptoms every week, and seven said they dealt with neck pain almost every day, highlighting how common the condition has become among desk-based workers.
Shashank, 38 years old media professional, said that he suffers neck stiffness, shoulder pain and arm pain very frequently.
âI spend around 8 hours sitting every day on a chair which does not provide good support to my neck. I believe more frequent breaks and awareness about the right furniture in the offices can help employees work more efficiently. Bad furniture set up leads to poor posture which ultimately results in all kinds of problems,â he told TOI.
Dr Arun Bhanot, Director â Spine Surgery at CK Birla Hospital, Gurugram, said there has been a noticeable rise in younger patients with desk jobs seeking treatment for neck pain.
"The profile of patients has shifted dramatically. Earlier, it was mostly older people with degenerative changes. Now, we are seeing a steady stream of people in their late 20s and 30s," he said.
Long hours at the desk were the norm, with 21 respondents spending more than eight hours seated every day, while another seven reported sitting for seven to eight hours.
Despite prolonged screen time, regular movement was uncommon. Twelve respondents said they rarely took breaks during work, while 10 stepped away from their desks only once every two to three hoursâfar less frequently than doctors recommend.
Komal Gupta, 30-year-old journalist, while talking to TOI, said that she hardly gets enough time to exercise regularly, even though she knows it would help reduce her neck pain.
âMost workdays are packed with deadlines, so taking out time for stretching or a workout becomes difficult.â
Dr Surender Pal Singh, HOD â Physiotherapy Department at CK Birla Hospital in Delhi advises keeping the monitor at eye level, ensuring proper chair support and avoiding carrying heavy laptop bags on one shoulder, as uneven weight distribution can increase stress on the neck and upper back.
However, most of the respondents responded with no furniture or equipment support from the employer.
Gupta said, âMy office also doesn't provide an external monitor or laptop stand, so I end up working directly on my laptop for long hours, which puts additional strain on my neck and shoulders.â
Problem not confined to corporate offices Jyoti Jaiswal, a 29-year-old dentist, says healthcare professionals are equally vulnerable due to the nature of their work.
"Treating patients often requires us to remain seated or stand in the same position for long periods, which puts considerable strain on the neck," she said.
Jaiswal believes better workload management could help reduce the problem. "Proper patient scheduling is essential so that sufficient time can be given to each patient without rushing or compromising body posture. It would also give doctors brief breaks between consultations, reducing physical strain," she added.
Tushar Gaur, a 25-year-old accountant from Meerut, says his job requires him to spend long hours seated, entering financial data and working continuously on a computer.
"The prolonged sitting and constant screen time often cause severe pain on the left side of my neck. I've realised that taking regular breaks helps reduce the discomfort, but during busy workdays it's not always possible," he said.
Dr Bhanot said, "The head weighs around 4.5 to 5 kilograms in a neutral position. But tilt it forward by just 15 degrees to look at a screen and the effective load on the cervical spine rises sharply. Hold that posture for eight hours a day, five days a week, and the muscles and ligaments simply give in."
Recalling one of his cases of treating a 26-year-old software developer, he said, â he developed severe neck pain, numbness in her fingers and forward-head posture after working from bed for nearly a year with her laptop balanced on a pillow.
"There was no disc herniation, but significant muscle strain. With ergonomic correction, physiotherapy and scheduled movement breaks, she was largely symptom-free within six weeks," he said.
So what can be done?Respondents overwhelmingly felt that preventing cervical pain requires both individual lifestyle changes and employer support. Many said companies should invest in ergonomic workstations, including better chairs, adjustable desks, laptop stands and the option of standing desks to reduce strain caused by prolonged sitting.
Several respondents also called for more employee-friendly workplace policies, such as reduced working hours, flexible schedules and better workload management to allow employees enough time to rest, exercise and maintain proper posture.
Others suggested that employers should encourage frequent breaks, with some even recommending software-based reminders or applications that temporarily lock screens every 30 minutes to prompt employees to stand up, stretch and move around.
While the other things are not in our hands, taking some time to exercise is.
Dr Singh stresses that prevention is often simple but overlooked. "Standing up, stretching and walking for just one or two minutes every 30 minutes can significantly reduce pressure on the neck and back," he said, adding that even the best workstation cannot prevent neck strain if a person remains seated for long hours without regular movement.
Every notification, meeting and deadline keeps employees glued to their desks. Yet, taking just a couple of minutes to move every half hour could make the difference between a healthy spine and years of chronic pain. In a workplace increasingly driven by productivity, perhaps the next big investment isn't technologyâit's healthier employees.
Because the next deadline can wait, your health canât.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: 
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday as Union education minister, taking moral responsibility for the NEET-UG paper leak controversy that has shaken the country's examination system, sparked mass student protests and triggered political confrontations.
In his resignation letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Pradhan said he had dedicated more than four decades to students, teachers and education reform.
He said the government had acted immediately after irregularities surfaced in the NEET-UG examination held on May 3, including cancelling the test, ordering a 
CBI probe and deciding to hold a fresh examination. He also said the test would be conducted in computer-based mode from next year.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
Pradhan said that he had tried from the first day to ensure that no meritorious student suffered because of what he described as an examination mafia. He said the unrest at Jantar Mantar and across the country had saddened him and that he was resigning to prevent anti-national forces from exploiting the situation and to protect the unity of the country.
Also Read | 
Dharmendra Pradhan resigns as Union education minister amid massive student protestsThe Odisha-born BJP leader had served as education minister since 2021 and was reappointed after the BJPâs victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha election.
Cockroach Janta Party chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the party had been called for third round of talks and would stay until a written commitment was made. He described the expected outcome as a 'huge victory'.
Click here to follow live blog updatesHere are the key events that led to the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan:Leak sparks outrage
The crisis began after allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination, which was held on May 3. Investigators later said a question set described as a 'guess paper' had circulated among students weeks before the test and that many questions closely matched the actual paper.
The National Testing Agency cancelled the exam on May 12 and the government referred the case to the Central Bureau of Investigation for a full probe. The exam, which is used for admission to undergraduate medical and dental courses, had been taken by nearly 22.79 lakh students. The cancellation marked the first full scrapping of 
NEET in its 13-year history.
Also Read | 
Watch: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke falls on stage after being told Dharmendra Pradhan has resignedThe government later announced that the re-examination would be held on June 21 and that no fresh registration would be required. It also said fees already paid would be refunded and that the exam would be shifted to online mode from 2027.
CBI widens probe
The CBI widened its investigation rapidly, carrying out searches at dozens of locations across several states and tracing the alleged source of leaked Physics, Chemistry and Biology questions. The agency said it had identified a network of accused persons, coaching links and middlemen involved in circulating the questions.
Among those arrested were a Latur-based doctor, Dr Manoj Shirure and a Pune-based physics faculty member, Tejas Harshadkumar Shah. Investigators said Dr Shirure helped three students access leaked Chemistry questions, while Shah allegedly passed on Physics questions obtained from another accused already in custody.
Earlier, the CBI had also arrested a Chemistry lecturer, PV Kulkarni, whom it described as a key figure in the leak. The agency said he had conducted special coaching sessions at his residence in Pune, where questions and answers were dictated and later matched the actual NEET paper.
Protest movement grows
The exam controversy soon became a major student movement. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical youth-led campaign, began protests at Jantar Mantar on June 20, demanding Pradhanâs resignation and accountability over paper leaks and other examination irregularities.
The agitation gathered pace after climate activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the protest and began an indefinite hunger strike. His deteriorating health drew wide attention on social media and his later hospitalisation further fuelled public anger. He eventually ended his 26-day hunger strike after receiving written assurances from the government.
The CJP said the movement would continue until Pradhan resigned. Its leaders also demanded compensation for the families of students who died by suicide, withdrawal of FIRs against peaceful protesters and a written guarantee that no such cases would be filed in future.
Centre shifts strategy
The Centreâs response changed over time. At first, several BJP leaders dismissed the protests, but the government later opened negotiations and announced a series of measures to calm the situation.
PM Modi said paper leaks were not an ordinary matter and announced fast-track courts to ensure swift punishment for those involved. He also said the government had acted to make sure that nearly 22 lakh students did not lose an academic year.
The Union Cabinet later approved amendments to anti-paper-leak law, proposing a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine of up to Rs 10 crore and a higher minimum sentence. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the Bill would be brought to Parliament soon.
At the same time, the National Testing Agency began a major internal overhaul, terminating 47 officials and recruiting new personnel in cybersecurity, digital forensics and test-centre operations. Officials said the changes were aimed at restoring confidence and tightening examination security.
Talks remain deadlocked
Even as the government expanded its response, its talks with the CJP remained unresolved. A second round of discussions between Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh and CJP representatives ended without a breakthrough. The CJP said the Centre had sought time until Saturday afternoon to respond to its main demand for Pradhanâs resignation.
The group said the other two major demandscompensation for bereaved families and withdrawal of cases against peaceful protesters had been accepted in principle. But it insisted that any further meeting must be held at a neutral venue, such as the Constitution Club of India, rather than a ministerâs residence.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi renewed his attack on the government, accusing Pradhan of presiding over a collapse of the education system. He also joined opposition leaders in paying tribute to students who died by suicide over the controversy and accused the Centre of using force against peaceful demonstrators.
Opposition steps up pressure
As protests spread across the country, opposition parties intensified their demand for Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, accusing the Centre of failing to protect the integrity of competitive examinations.
Parliament witnessed repeated disruptions as INDIA bloc MPs insisted that the education minister step down before any discussion on the NEET controversy could begin.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi emerged as one of the strongest critics of the government, calling Pradhan 'a symbol of the collapse of our education system' and saying, "He has to go." He also said students were making three key demands: the education minister's removal, action against those responsible for the alleged pellet gun use and lathi-charge on protesters, and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the affected youth.
The opposition also organised protests and candlelight marches in solidarity with students and families affected by the alleged paper leak and exam-related suicides.
Rahul Gandhi later brought before the media a protester whom he claimed had suffered pellet gun injuries during the Jantar Mantar demonstration, alleging that the government had falsely denied using pellet guns against protesters. "His eye has suffered damage, and he has lost his vision," Gandhi said, while accusing the Centre of attacking the future of the country's youth instead of addressing their concerns.
Courts and Parliament
The Supreme Court agreed to hear petitions over alleged excessive police action against protesters. The court also clarified that reports saying it had refused to hear the matter were false.
Parliament too was paralysed repeatedly as opposition MPs pressed for Pradhanâs resignation before any debate could begin. The government said it was ready for discussion without preconditions and accused the opposition of blocking parliamentary proceedings.
Meanwhile, Delhi Police warned that those directly involved in violence during the protests could face passport cancellation. The warning came after clashes near Jantar Mantar left several police personnel and protesters injured.
What the resignation means
Pradhanâs resignation is the biggest political consequence so far of the NEET controversy. It follows weeks of criticism over repeated exam irregularities, the handling of protests and the governmentâs initial response, which opponents said was too slow and dismissive.
The CBI probe into the alleged leak has widened across several states, with arrests made and searches carried out in multiple cities. The case has also prompted the government to push a tougher anti-paper leak law, while the National Testing Agency has begun a major overhaul of its staffing and security arrangements.

full_text:
Nepal has formally requested India's approval to recognise its biometric National Identity (NID) card as an official travel document for cross-border journeys, alongside passports and citizenship certificates.
At present, Nepali citizens travelling to India, particularly by air, must carry either a valid passport or an original citizenship certificate. Indian citizens entering Nepal are required to present either a passport or an original voter identity card with a photograph.
However, Nepal's National Identity card contains biometric information, including fingerprints, facial images and iris scans. The programme was launched as a pilot in Panchthar district and among government employees in 2009. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
So far, more than 4.5 million Nepali citizens have received the card, while nearly 20 million applications have been submitted.
Nepal plans to replace citizenship certificatesThe request comes as Nepal gradually makes the biometric National Identity card mandatory for banking, land registration, passport issuance and access to public services, with plans to eventually replace citizenship certificates.
"In the long run, we will have a single identity card replacing the citizenship certificate. 
It is verified, authentic and technology-friendly," Tiwari said.
"That is why we have requested India to allow the use of the National Identity Card while travelling by both air and land routes," he added.
India reviews the proposalAccording to senior immigration officials quoted by 
The Kathmandu Post, an Indian Embassy delegation met officials from Nepal's Department of Immigration earlier this week to discuss the proposal
The delegation was reportedly "positive" about the initiative and informed Nepalese officials that the request had been forwarded to authorities in New Delhi for consideration.
"We have already forwarded the proposal to the Indian side through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs," said Ram Chandra Tiwari, Director General of the Department of Immigration.
Officials from Nepal's Home Ministry also said that discussions have included creating formal mechanisms to record cross-border travel data and better manage movement between the two neighbouring countries.
